headline: Chip Wreckage and Strait Uncertainty Cloud the Open
body_html:
Futures traders are navigating a treacherous backdrop this Wednesday morning after Tuesday's session delivered one of the sharpest semiconductor selloffs in recent memory. The chip complex bore the brunt of the pain, with the Semiconductors sector shedding more than six percent on the day — a decline that dragged breadth deeply negative across our 550-name universe, where decliners outpaced advancers by nearly two to one at 358 versus 190.

The geopolitical overhang shows little sign of lifting before the open. Iran has signaled that the Strait of Hormuz will remain effectively closed until Washington meets interim negotiating conditions, a posture that continued to push oil prices higher overnight. Slowing tanker traffic through the waterway is tightening near-term supply expectations, and energy traders will be watching any diplomatic signals out of Washington and Tehran closely. Compounding the tension, France announced plans to expel two Iranian diplomats, while U.S. prosecutors unsealed charges against seventeen individuals linked to an Iran-backed hacking operation.

Treasury yields, which surged Tuesday and contributed to the equity selloff, have edged modestly lower in overnight trading — offering tentative relief. Software and Healthcare managed slim gains in Tuesday's session, suggesting some rotation appetite exists. At the open, the key question is whether that defensive bid can offset renewed pressure in rate-sensitive and growth-oriented sectors.

briefs.headline: Fabrinet Leads Optical Rout With Nearly 20% Plunge
briefs.body: Fabrinet cratered 19.38% on Tuesday, the steepest single-session loss in our universe, dragging the broader optical and networking sub-sectors sharply lower. Coherent fell 12.75% in sympathy, underscoring how concentrated the selling pressure became in high-bandwidth interconnect names as the chip complex broadly unraveled.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Closure Threat Keeps Oil on the Boil
briefs.body: Iran reiterated that transit through the Strait of Hormuz will remain restricted pending U.S. concessions on interim deal terms. Tanker traffic through the waterway has visibly slowed, and crude prices extended gains overnight. Energy markets will be the primary macro variable to monitor at Wednesday's open.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Posts Its Worst Day in Recent Memory
briefs.body: The Semiconductors sector dropped 6.16% on Tuesday, far outpacing losses in any other group. MaxLinear fell 14.31%, Credo Technology shed 13.03%, Semtech declined 12.31%, and Allegro MicroSystems lost nearly 11% — a synchronized wave of selling that suggests institutional de-risking rather than isolated earnings events.

briefs.headline: DOJ Charges Seventeen in Iran-Linked Cyber Campaign
briefs.body: Federal prosecutors unsealed indictments against seventeen individuals alleged to have participated in a hacking operation attributed to Iranian state backing. The move adds a new legal dimension to an already strained U.S.-Iran relationship and arrives as diplomatic channels remain under acute stress over the Hormuz situation.

briefs.headline: Insulet and Ulta Shine as Defensive Bids Find Footing
briefs.body: Insulet Corporation advanced 5.96% and Ulta Beauty gained 4.75% on Tuesday, each bucking the broader selloff as investors sought shelter in healthcare-device and consumer-beauty names. The divergence from the tape highlights selective rotation into companies perceived as less exposed to semiconductor supply-chain and rate pressures.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders and Industrials Buckle as Yields Spike
briefs.body: Rising Treasury yields weighed heavily on rate-sensitive sectors Tuesday, with Homebuilders falling 1.83% and Industrials dropping 2.11%. Both groups are acutely sensitive to financing costs and broader economic confidence. With yields edging only modestly lower overnight, neither sector is likely to see immediate relief at Wednesday's open.
